perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s subjective perspective, he has access to the following information:

- He and Jonathan Balogun have been close friends since childhood. Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian has recently felt anxious and suspicious that Jonathan is hiding something important. He has observed Jonathan acting differently.
- Christian arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something serious.
- Christian heard Jonathan say that Christian could trust him, but then Jonathan admitted he had been keeping something from him: Jonathan is in some kind of trouble and did not know how to tell Christian.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered to help Jonathan and said they could face whatever it was together.
- Christian heard Jonathan say the situation is complicated, that he did not want to drag Christian into it, and that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian asked Jonathan whether the trouble was related to anything illegal.
- Christian heard Jonathan say he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into the matter discreetly to make sure Jonathan is safe. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe that Jonathan is being framed by someone.
- Christian told Jonathan he believed Jonathan was being framed, that he had some leads, and that he planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian heard Jonathan express surprise and gratitude.
- Christian came to believe or found out that the real culprit is someone close to both him and Jonathan. He told Jonathan this, said he would confront the person, and said the betrayal would not go unpunished.
- Christian heard Jonathan warn him that the person is dangerous, but also say that he trusts Christian to do what is right.

Christian does not have access to private thoughts, hidden events, or narrator-only facts beyond what he personally observed, was told, or discovered through his own investigation.
